svg.text: From each sample's copy-number segments (hg19; autosomes only — X's log ratio mostly records sex), computed per sample in the database: FGA is the share of the
sample's segmented length whose |segment mean| is at or past 0.2 (log2), counted in 1-point bins; an arm (p and q split at hg19's centromeres, from UCSC's cytoBand;
the acrocentric p arms of 13, 14, 15, 21 and 22 left out, as Taylor et al. 2018 did) is gained or lost when more than 50% of its length is past ±0.2, and the aneuploidy
score is how many of the 39 arms are. Colorectal: 5,273 samples scored of 5,277 (5,273 with segments; 5,237 with every arm covered); Breast: 6,806 samples scored of
6,807 (6,806 with segments; 6,587 with every arm covered); Pancreatic: 2,850 samples scored of 2,851 (2,850 with segments; 2,832 with every arm covered); an arm
segments cover for less than 50% of its length is not called, which lowers that sample's score. Boxes are the quartiles, whiskers the 5th and 95th percentiles, read from
the histograms; Kruskal–Wallis compares the cohorts' distributions (normal approximation with ties). Every sample of the cohort counts. Panel-derived segments are
noisy and purity is not corrected — a low-purity tumour's changes sit near 0 and read as stable — so these are relative measures within one assay, not absolute ploidy.
